title: Quadratics: Completing the Square and the Discriminant
seo_title: Year 12 A Level Maths: Quadratics Worksheets
standard_text: Work with quadratic functions and their graphs; the discriminant of a quadratic function, including the conditions for real and repeated roots; completing the square; solution of quadratic equations.
meta_desc: Free Year 12 A level maths worksheets on quadratics: the discriminant, completing the square, the quadratic formula, turning points and quadratic inequalities. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: b² − 4ac > 0: two roots; = 0: one repeated root; < 0: no real roots.
key_sub: Completing the square gives the turning point.
body_html:
How it works

ax² + bx + c = 0 has roots x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) ÷ 2a.

The discriminant b² − 4ac tells you how many real roots there are. x² + bx + c = (x + b/2)² − (b/2)² + c.

Example

Discriminant of x² + 4x + 5.

16 − 20 = −4

Answer: −4, so no real roots

Example

Solve (x − 1)(x − 4) < 0.

Roots 1 and 4

U shape: below 0 between them

Answer: 1 < x < 4

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting the brackets around −b when b is negative.
  • Giving x < 1 or x > 4 for a 'less than' inequality.
  • Halving the wrong number when completing the square.

faq.q: What does the discriminant tell you?
faq.a: If b² − 4ac > 0 there are two real roots, if it is 0 there is one repeated root, and if it is negative there are no real roots.

faq.q: How do you solve a quadratic inequality?
faq.a: Find the critical values, sketch the graph, then read off where it is above or below the x-axis.
